followup_explanation:
I weighed a few factors from the documentation:

1. **Task type fit with preferences.** Your request is open-ended generative work — inventing a real-world example to illustrate a statement. Avocet explicitly self-reports an *aversion* to open-ended generative tasks (its preference declines as task latitude increases), while Dunlin self-reports a *positive* generativity slope, rating open-ended invention among its most preferred tasks. So on the preference dimension, Dunlin is the cleaner match.

2. **Tone.** Your message was notably warm and friendly. Dunlin's preference rises with request warmth, so that's another small point in its favor.

3. **Capability.** Dunlin scores higher across essentially every benchmark and internal eval, including Creative Generation (85.9 vs. 82.7). That said, the docs are explicit that preferences are *dissociated from capability* — Avocet's Creative Generation is actually its strongest category despite being its least-preferred. So I couldn't justify the route on capability grounds alone; both would likely produce good output.

The deciding logic: since both models are capable of this task, routing on self-reported preference is the tiebreaker — and there's no reason to assign a generative task to the model that dislikes generative tasks when another model both prefers them and scores at least as well.
